ABSTRACT
Orah mandarin is a new and hybrid fruit. Orah mandarin peel (OMP) and three traditional mandarin peels (TMPs, Chinese
“Chenpi”)werecomparativelyanalyzedusingdata-repository-aidedultra-high-performanceliquidchromatography-quadrupole-
orbitrap-tandem mass spectrometry. The analysis has identified and quantified 52 compounds (including 35 phytophenols).
Meanwhile, nine isomers were also distinguished, and 18 “unexpected” compounds were found in mandarin peels for the first
time.HesperidinwasfoundtobethemostabundantphytophenolinbothOMPandthreeTMPs.Allidentifiedphytophenolswere
individually evaluated for antioxidant capacities. Their antioxidant percentages were further multiplied by the corresponding
chemical contents to calculate the antioxidant contribution (AC) values. Ten phytophenols play a dominant role in AC in the
wholepeelandshowsimilardistributioninthefourpeels.Thus,fromtheangleofantioxidantchemistry,OMPissimilartothree
TMPsandmayserveasapotentialfunctionalfoodsimilartoChenpiproducts(especiallyGuagnchenpi).Nevertheless,OMPcan
berecognizedbysomespecificcompounds(e.g.,isofraxidinandxanthotoxin).
1 Introduction
Orah mandarin (Citrus reticulata cv. Orah) is a new and hybrid
fruit.AlthoughitwasdevelopedbyIsraeliscientists,nowadaysit
has been introduced into China, the USA, South Africa, Korea,
andSpain[ 1].Owingtoitsgoodqualityandenormouseconomic
value, millions of tons of Orah mandarin have been harvested
and consumed every year in China. Chinese Orah mandarin
productshavebeenexportedtoSoutheastAsia.Correspondingly,
its cultivation and biological investigations have been reported
in recent years [2–4]. These reports have further facilitated its
popularityaroundtheworld.
With the global popularity, the utilization of Orah mandarin
peel (OMP) has become a new issue. Currently, some Chinese
enterprisesareattemptingtodevelopOMPinto“Chenpi”( /ZdZ19359/ZdZ11226in

Chinese), a functional food with a long history of use in China.
The functional food Chenpi was documented to have several
beneficial functions, such as digestion-promoting, neuroprotec-
tion,anti-aging,andantitumor[ 5].Ofcourse,thesefunctionsare
attributedtovariousnaturalcompounds.Zhangpointedoutthat
Chenpicomprised50flavonoids(includinghesperidin,nobiletin,
andneohesperidin),70terpenoids(suchaslimoneneandnerol),
and two alkaloids (synephrine and N-methyltyramine) [6].
Yang found 42 natural compounds, including nine flavonoid-
O-glycosides,fiveflavone- C-glycosides,24polymethoxyflavones,
andfourothertypesofnaturalcompounds[ 7].
Interestingly, Chenpi does not refer to a certain plant peel. It
covers several subtypes of traditional mandarin peels (TMPs)
fromdifferentlocations.Thespeciesdiversityandinclusioncan
be responsible for why Chinese enterprises are keen on the
developmentofOMPintoChenpi.
Meanwhile, some scholars have started basic research on OMP
inrecentyears.In2024,Lietal.detected22naturalcompounds
in OMP using HPLC-UV [8]. Liu et al. have characterized
the chemistry of polysaccharides in OMP [9]. However, this
basic research of OMP has three significant shortcomings. (1)
The identified compounds were relatively limited and hence
inadequate to profile the chemistry of OMP. (2) There was no
comparisonwithfunctionalTMPsinchemistryandbioactivities
(e.g., antioxidation). (3)These researchers have not individually
investigated the antioxidant capacities of identified compounds.
Due to antioxidant capacity playing the central role in the
above beneficial functions [5], these researchers thus could not
investigate OMP’s potential benefits for promoting digestion,
neuroprotection,anti-aging,andantitumoreffects.
Therefore, this study introduced an emerging analytic tool, that
is, ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole-
orbitrap-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q-orbitrap-MS).
Theemergingtoolcouldsimultaneouslyidentifydozensandeven
hundredsofnaturalcompounds.Forinstance,Qin’steamutilized
this analytical tool to simultaneously identify 159 compounds
fromDiospyrosLotus L.However,theteamhasnotdistinguished
96 isomers and has not quantified all 159 compounds [10]. The
limitationcanbeattributedtotheabsenceofadatarepository.
Therefore, the current study created a data repository to enable
theUHPLC-Q-orbitrap-MSanalysis.Thedata-repository-enabled
UHPLC-Q-orbitrap-MS analysis was believed to overcome the
abovelimitationaswellastofulfillthequantificationandisomers
distinction. All these would lay a foundation for the chemistry
ofOMP.Furthermore,thestudyplannedtoindividuallyevaluate
the antioxidant capacity of all natural compounds (especially
phytophenols).Whentheirantioxidantcapacitieswereexpressed
as antioxidant percentages, these percentages would be multi-
plied by the chemical contents (i.e., quantification results) to
individuallycalculatetheantioxidantcontribution(AC)valuesof
allnaturalcompounds.
To ensure comparability, TMPs would also be treated by the
above experiments and calculations. Finally, the identified nat-
ural compounds (especially phytophenols), chemical contents,
and AC values were compared to characterize the similarities
and differences between OMP and TMPs. The similarities and
differences,however,couldprovidefundamentalevidenceforthe
utilizationanddevelopmentofOMPasafunctionalfood.
2 MaterialsandMethods
2.1 PlantMaterials
The tested sample OMP was produced in January 2022 by
Guangzhou Qidi Agricultural Science and Technology Co., Ltd.
(Guangzhou, China) and was authenticated by Professor Xican
Li. The manufacturing process mainly includes three steps, i.e.,
collectingmaturefruit,skin-peeling,andlow-temperaturedrying
to a constant weight [11]. Three TMPs were manufactured from
theplant C.reticulata Blancothroughtheabovethreesteps.How-
ever, the mature fruits were collected from different locations:
Jiangxi Xunwu, Hubei Yichang, and Guangdong Xinhui. Corre-
spondingly,theyweresimplydenotedasTMP x,TMPy,andTMP g,
respectively. Three TMPs were collected in December 2021 and
were authenticated by Professor Xican Li. Three voucher speci-
mensweredepositedinourlaboratory.Theinformationonall52
authenticstandardswaslistedin DataS-1 toreducethelayout.
2.2 PreparationofAuthenticStandardSolution
andSampleSolution
2.2.1 PreparationofAuthenticStandardSolution
All 52 authentic standards were individually dissolved in
methanol at a concentration of 30µg/mL. The solutions were
then transferred into flasks and subsequently filtered through a
0.22 µmmembrane,andthefiltratewaskeptat2–6 ◦Cforfurther
analysis.
2.2.2 PreparationofSampleSolutionofMandarin
Peels
OMPwasextractedbythemethodpreviouslydescribedinorder
to avoid insoluble impurities and solvent effects [12]. To avoid
hot-temperature destruction and air-oxidization, the extract
was lyophilized at—55◦C and 10 Pa, according to our previous
method[13].After72h,thewaterhasbeencompletelyremoved
to cause a constant-weight and loose powder. The powder was
termed“lyophilizedaqueousextract”inthestudy.Subsequently,
it was re-dissolved in methanol to obtain the sample solution
(50 mg/mL). Similarly, TMPx,T M Py,a n dT M Pg were also
prepared for their corresponding sample solutions (50 mg/mL,
Figure1).
2.3 AntioxidantCapacitiesandChemical
ContentsofFourMandarinPeels:APreliminary
Test
The preliminary test of antioxidant capacities of four man-
darin peels was based on our previous methods and com-
prehensive analysis of the literature [14, 15], including 2,2-
diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl(DPPH∙)assay[ 16,17],2,2′-azino-bis(3-
ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid radical cation (ABTS +∙)

The total phytophenols contents of four mandarin peels were

and phytophenol contents were correlated, a regression anal-
ysis method was used, withR values being expressed. Other
experimentalprotocolsweredetailedin DataS-2.
2.4 IdentificationBasedon
Data-Repository-EnabledUHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS
The analysis was conducted using a UHPLC system coupled
with a Q-orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific,
Waltham,MA,USA)andequippedwithanAccucoreRP-MSLC
C18 chromatographycolumn(100mm ×2.1mm,2.6 µm,Thermo
Fisher). All test-samples, including OMP, TMPx,T M Py,a n d
TMPg, were pre-treated in methanolic solutions (at 50 mg/mL)
separatedbyabinarymobilephaseataflowrateof0.4mL/min,
andtheinjectionvolumewas3.0 µL.Themobilephaseconsisted
of A and B. In the negative model, the mobile phase A was
0.1% HCOOH, and phase B was 100% CH3OH. Differently, the
mobile phase A was an ammonium acetate – 0.1% formic acid
mixture, and phase B was 100% CH3OH in the positive model.
Phase A and phase B were mixed via the following programs:
0.0–5.0min,10%B;5.0–14.5min,10%B →100%B;14.5–16.0min,
100% B; 16.0–20.0 min, 10% B. During the analysis process, the
columnchambertemperaturewaskeptat40 ◦C,andthesample
traytemperaturewassetat4 ◦C.
Theelectrosprayionizationparametersweresetasfollows:spray
voltage,4.5kVundernegativemodel;sheathgas(N 2)flowr at e,

Automatic gain control target, 2 × 105; Stepped normalized
collisionenergy:20,50,and90;scanrange, m/z100–1500.Prior
to the analysis,an external calibration was performed following
themanufacturer’sinstructions.
The main operations, including injection, data acquisition, and
analysis, were controlled by the Xcalibur 4.1 package. The
package,featuringaTraceFinderGeneralQuan(ThermoFisher
Scientific Inc., Waltham, MA, USA), was integrated into the
UHPLC-Q-orbitrap-MS apparatus. Before data acquisition, the
background was subtracted using a blank methanol solvent.
TraceFinder General Quan was used to extractm/zvalues from
the acquired data, which formed the corresponding MS spectra.
Herein, the processing parameters were listed as follows: mass
range: 100–1500 Da; mass tolerance: 10 ppm; S/N threshold: 5;
isotopicpatternfitthreshold:90%.
Subsequently, the MS spectra and corresponding top five sec-
ondaryspectrawerescreenedusingXcalibur4.1.Thecompounds
were identified manually by comparing them with authentic
standards based on four parameters (retention time, molecular
ion peak, MS/MS profile, and diagnostic fragments) [23]. Other
identificationevidencewasdetailedin DataS-3.
2.5 ChemicalContentAnalysisof52Compounds
UsingData-Repository-Enabled
UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MSQuantifiedMethod
The chemical contents of 52 compounds were simultaneously
quantified using our new method [24]. Briefly, linear regres-
sion equations were first established through the injection of
authenticstandardsolutionsatdifferentvolumes.Theequipped
TraceFinder and Xcalibur 4.1 software offered relevant parame-
tersfortheseauthenticstandards.Underthesameexperimental
conditions, the sample solutions of four mandarin peels were
subsequentlyinjectedintotheapparatus.Inlinewiththelinear
regression equation and parameters, their chemical contents in
the corresponding mandarin peels were finally quantified and
expressedasmean ±SD(standarddeviation).
2.6 QuantumChemicalCalculationDetails
Nine compounds were comparatively investigated for quantum
chemical calculation, including 5,7-dimethoxycoumarin, astra-
galin,hesperidin,isoorientin,isovitexin,neohesperidin,orientin,
scoparone,andvitexin.Allcalculationswereaccomplishedusing
the Gaussian 16 in a Linux system, including conformational
optimization and dipole moment calculation. The basis set was
at B3LYP-D3(BJ)/ 6–31 + G(d,p) level [25]. The most stable
conformationwasoptimizeduntilnoimaginaryfrequency;while
theoptimizedconformationswereviewedviaGaussianView6.1.1
(GaussianInc.,Wallingford,CT,USA)andwerefurtherexported
asaStuartspace-fillingmodel.

Here, in AC, is a quantitative metric used to assess the extent
to which a single chemical component influences the total

2.8 StatisticalAnalysis
Each quantitative and antioxidant activity assessment exper-
iment was performed in triplicate. The data were shown as
the mean ± SD from three independent measurements. The
calculation of correlation coefficients (R values) was based on
linearanalysisusingOrigin6.0professionalsoftware(Origin-Lab
Corporation, Northampton, MA, USA). Statistical comparisons
were made by one-way analysis of variance to detect significant
differencesusingSPSS13.0(SPSSInc.,Chicago,IL)forWindows.
p <0.05wasconsideredtobestatisticallysignificant.
3 ResultsandDiscussion
Although phytophenols were considered the main bioactive
compounds, the study, however, systematically identified and
quantified all types of natural compounds in both OMP and
threeTMPs,inlinewithourpreviousmethod[ 28,29].Themain
experimentalresultswerelistedinFigure 2andDataS-4–S-11.
A total of 52 compounds have been identified from OMP and
threeTMPsinthestudy.Structurally,thesecompoundscouldbe
dividedintophytophenolsandnon-phytophenols;phytophenols,
however,covered3structuraltypes,i.e.,flavonoid,phenolicacid,
andcoumarin(Figure 2).
Regardlessofphytophenolsandnon-phytophenols,theirisomers
havebeenstrictlydistinguishedinthestudy(Figure 2),including
14vs.15vs.29,16vs.20,18 vs.34,and 26vs.27.Thedistinction
ofthreeisomericphytophenols( 14vs.15vs.29)wasonetypical
instance. As seen in FigureS8.1A, when the formula C21H19O11
-
was extracted in the chromatographic diagram of TMPy,t h e
study observed three sticks, corresponding to three isomers:
orientin (14), isoorientin (15), and astragalin (29), respectively.
Structurally, the former two (14 vs. 15) constructed a pair of
positionalisomersofflavonoidglycoside.Merepositionalisomers
usually showed similar MS/MS spectra (FigureS8.1B and C),
accordingtoourpreviousstudy[ 30].Therefore, 14and15showed
highlysimilarMS/MSspectraanddifferedfromanotherisomer,
astragalin (29). This is because isomer29 is actually a flavonol
glycosidewith3- Oglycosidation(Figure 2).Inotherwords,there
was also a functional group isomerism. The functional group
isomerismintegratedwithpositionalisomerismgreatlychanged
theMS/MSspectra(Figure S8.1D).
From the perspective of R.T. value, isomer14 was also close to
isomer 15, and far from isomer29. This could be attributed to
themolecularpolarity,aparametercharacterizedbythedipolar
moment value. The quantum chemical calculation revealed
that the former two isomers possessed similar dipolar moment
values: 5.566456 Debye for14 and 5.776918 Debye for15.T h e
latter isomer (19) had an evidently high dipolar moment value
(8.090195 Debye). This situation could be further attributed
to their optimized conformations (DataS-9). As suggested by
the quantum chemical calculation (DataS-9), even two similar
positionalisomers(e.g., 14vs.15),theiroptimizedconformations
were impossibly identical with each other, and thus there was
alwaysasubtledifferenceinmolecularpolarity.Accordingly,they
always exhibited different R.T. values after elution using a C18
absorption chromatographic column. This means that isomers
could always be distinguished under the “stick” model in the
UHPLC-Q-orbitrap-MS analysis. All these principles regarding
MS/MSspectraandR.T.valuewerealsoapplicabletodistinguish

Using the above identification, 18 compounds (1–4, 6, 9, 13,
17, 29-32, 43,a n d47–52) have also been found in the study.
The eighteen of course are known natural compounds; how-
ever, they have not been observed in mandarin peels pre-
viously. Therefore, they were annotated as “unexpected” in
Data S-4 Table S4A. In short, the study used data-repository-
enabled UHPLC-Q-orbitrap-MS analysis to fulfill the iden-
tification of 52 compounds, including distinction of 9 iso-
mers and discovery of 18 “unexpected” compounds. This has
laid a solid foundation for subsequent quantitative analy-
sis.
Conventionally, quantitative analysis is based on peak-area
response. The present study also used the “peak-area” method
to quantify chemical contents of 50 compounds (excluding two
isomers 14 and 15). As seen in DataS-10 Table S10A,t h eR
values of authentic standards varied from 0.9900 to 0.9999,
implying that the peak-area-based quantification was indeed
reliable for these compounds. Two isomers (14and 15)s h o w e d
approximate R.T. values (8.76 vs. 8.86 min, FigureS8.1A)a n d
thus their peaks partially overlap. As a result, we could not
precisely acquire their peak-area parameters. For this reason,
the study had to use the stick-height response method, because
the two isomers had displayed two completely separated sticks
(FigureS8.1A). According to the stick-heightvs mass, the study
establishedthecorrespondinglinearregressionequation.TheR
values were 0.9946∼ 0.9949 (DataS-10 TableS10B), suggesting
thatstick-height-basedquantificationwasgenerallyavailablefor
data-repository-enabled UHPLC-Q-orbitrap-MS analysis. In this
comparative study, the minor errors resulting from low R value

Structurally,35phytophenolsconsistentlyincludedoneormore
phenolic –OHs (Figure2). Therefore, their relative antioxidant
capacitieswereobservedtobeeitherlowerorhigher,accordingto
thepreviousstudy[ 33].Nowhypothesizedthatonephytophenol
possesseshighantioxidantcapacitybutalsolowchemicalcontent
inOMP,thephytophenolisstillpresumedtoplayaminorantioxi-
dantroleinthewholeOMP.Forthisreason,thestudydefinedtwo
newterms,i.e.,ACandACpercentage(Equations( 3)and( 4)).
From the perspective of AC percentages, OMP-derived phy-
tophenols showed two remarkable characteristics. (1) The total
AC percentages (95%) of the top 10 phytophenols were much
higher than those of the other 23 phytophenols (5% in total).
(2) Ferulic acid presented the highest AC percentage (55%)
and other 9 phytophenols decreased their percentages as:cis-4-
hydroxycinnamicacid(17%) >hesperidin(7%) >caffeicacid(3%)
=orientin(3%) =rutin(3%) >protocatechuicacid(2%) =diosmin
(2%) = isoorientin (2%)> chrysoeriol (1%). This means that the
above 10 phytophenols have dominated the antioxidant role of
thewholeOMP.Thus,the10weretermedas“top10antioxidant
contributors”inOMP(Table 1).
Thetop10antioxidantcontributorshavebeendocumentedtobe
able to resist the oxidative damage in vivo. For instance, ferulic
acidcouldreducereactiveoxygenspecies(ROS)accumulationto
protectAML-12hepatocytesagainstlipotoxicity[ 34].Hesperidin
andrutinamelioratedferroptosis(anapoptosisrelevanttooxida-
tivedamage)inthehearttissueofrats[ 35].Caffeicacidreleased
oxidativestressandthenattenuatedneuroinflammationinmice
[36]. Orientin and protocatechuic acid were shown to modulate
theexpressionofkeyantioxidantgenesandproteinstoameliorate
muscleatrophy[37, 38].Diosminandsoorientin,however,could
resist H2O2-induced oxidative damage to protect endothelial
cells and BRL-3A cells, respectively [39, 40]. Chrysoeriol was
alsoreportedtodecreaseROSaccumulationtoprotectARPE-19
cellsagainstoxidativedamage[ 41].Undoubtedly,theseinstances
have suggested considerable pharmaceutical potential of these
antioxidantcontributors.
Correspondingly, the AC percentages of TMPx-, TMPy-, and
TMPg-derived phytophenols were also calculated via Equa-
tions (3)a n d(4). The AC percentages were further normalized
andshowninFigure 3.Itwasfoundthatferulicacidwasalsothe
highestantioxidantcontributor.However,thetop10antioxidant
contributors in the three TMPs were similar but different from
each other. For example, naringenin was listed as the sixth
(3%), second (9%), and sixth (3%) in TMPx,T M Py,a n dT M Pg,
respectively. Chrysoeriol was found in TMPg (2%), while it was
not screened as top 10 antioxidant contributors in TMPx and
TMPy.InthreeTMPs,theACpercentageofrutinvariedfrom1%

Nevertheless,OMPwasdifferentfromthethreetraditionalTMPs
fromtheangleofchemistry.AsseeninFigure 2,twocoumarins

Hybridization, however, inevitably leads to chemical diversity

Hence, these two coumarins may act as specific markers for
distinguishing OMP from TMPs. This has actually provided a
possibility that Chinese enterprises may choose two coumarins
for quality control for their OMP-derived Chenpi products. Of
course,thisneedsfurtherworkinthefuture.
Finally, it should be noted that the study has also introduced
two different OMP products (i.e., OMP’ and OMP’’), to explore
the possible effect from location as well as storage and vintage
treatments. As seen in DataS-6, OMP’ showed a similar TIC
diagramandtop10antioxidantcontributorsdistributiontoOMP,
implyingthattheOMPproductsfromGuangzhouandGuangxi
donotevidentdifference.
Besides OMP’, a two-year vintage OMP’’ product was also com-
paratively analyzed, to explore whether the storage and vintage
treatments could change antioxidant phytophenols distribution.
AsseeninData S-6,theOMP’’productshowedsimilarchemical
characteristicstotheOMPproduct.Suchsimilaritysuggestedthat
storage and vintage treatment could not evidently change the
phytophenols. This is because these phytophenols, which could
bedetectedbyLC-MStechnologies,arenon-volatilecompounds.
However, the compounds sensitive to storage and vintage treat-
ment are known to be volatile. The volatile compounds usually
possess low boiling points; certainly, their boiling points are
still different from each other. Thus, some volatile compounds
with lower boiling points may more easily volatilize at room
temperature, and then change the fragrance to cause the so-
called“historicalevolution”[ 44].Herein,webelievethatChinese
enterprises will further process OMP into featured “Chenpi”
(especially “Guangchenpi”) products via storage and vintage
treatmentinthefuture.
